subtype: Approach: accepting that the friendship is changing [Revision]
passage: Zeenat had promised to come to the district quiz final, and Gaurav waited at the school gate until the last auto had left. It was the third promise in two months. The next morning Zeenat said sorry, and seemed to mean it. Gaurav said it was fine, and noticed he had stopped saving a seat. Over the following weeks he sat with Farhan and Disha from the quiz club, went to football on Saturdays, and kept the small things with Zeenat: a hello at the lockers, a joke on the way to the lab. He did not make a speech or keep a score. It felt like a door closing quietly, a little sad, and oddly lighter.

qa.q: How many promises had Zeenat broken by the quiz final?
qa.a: The quiz final was the third promise in two months.

qa.q: What is Gaurav feeling as he stops saving a seat?
qa.a: Gaurav feels a little sad but lighter, since he has stopped waiting for closeness that did not come back.

qa.q: What other approach could Gaurav use if he wanted to try rebuilding?
qa.a: Gaurav could say calmly that kept promises matter to him and ask Zeenat for one small promise to keep, because one honest test shows if trust can return.

qa.q: How might Zeenat notice this change?
qa.a: Zeenat may feel puzzled or hurt by the growing distance, since there is no fight or blame to explain it.

grounding: After repeated broken promises the student sees trust has not returned, keeps a polite connection, invests in other friends and lets the closeness settle lower without blame.

subtype: Approach: accepting that the friendship is changing [Revision]
passage:
"Aman's not coming again?" Nandini asked, as Hemant put the second badminton racket back on the shelf.
"Third time this month. Said he'd be here at five."
"Are you going to fight with him about it?"
"I did, in September. He said sorry. Then he did it again." Hemant sat on the sofa. "I don't think he's doing it to hurt me. He's just... somewhere else now."
"That sounds sad."
"It is a bit." He shrugged. "But I'm not going to keep waiting by the door. I'll still say hi, still wish him on his birthday. I'm just not planning my Saturdays around him."
"So who are you playing with?"
"Joseph from tuition asked last week. I said maybe. I'm going to say yes."
Nandini handed him the racket back. "Go on, then."

qa.q: How many times this month has Aman not come?
qa.a: This is the third time this month.

qa.q: How does Hemant seem to feel about Aman?
qa.a: He seems sad and a little resigned, but not angry, believing Aman isn't trying to hurt him.

qa.q: Why is Hemant's plan healthier than fighting again?
qa.a: He already tried talking and the promises kept breaking, so staying polite while making time for new friends like Joseph protects him without blame.

qa.q: How does Nandini respond to Hemant's decision?
qa.a: Nandini is sympathetic, calling it sad, and then encourages him by handing back the racket.

grounding: A dialogue shows a boy accepting after repeated broken promises that a friendship has become less close, staying polite and turning to other friends.

subtype: Approach: accepting that the friendship is changing [Revision]
passage: I'm Karthik, and this year I stopped trying to make Preeti my best friend again. We'd been close since Class 4. Since she moved to the other section, she has cancelled on me again and again: the science fair we were doing together, my birthday lunch, Sunday cycling. Each time she said sorry, and meant it, I think. And each time it happened again. My Paati noticed I'd stopped checking my phone on Sundays. "Fighting with your friend, beta?" she asked. "No," I said, "just letting it be smaller." I still say hi, and we still laugh in the corridor. But I joined the robotics club, and Saturdays belong to them now. I don't blame her. People drift. It hurts a little less every month.

qa.q: How does Karthik feel about the drifting friendship?
qa.a: He feels a quiet sadness that hurts a little less every month, without anger or blame.
He keeps a friendly link with Preeti while putting his energy into robotics, so he isn't stuck waiting or blaming.

qa.q: How might Preeti experience the change?
qa.a: Preeti may barely notice at first, busy with the new section, and later sense that the closeness has settled lower without hard feelings.

grounding: A boy reflects on accepting, after repeated broken promises, that a friendship has become less close, keeping it polite and investing elsewhere.
